problem.concept: selecting a subset of relevant features in a potentially overwhelming quantity of data

problem.concept: natural language generation (NLG) component of a spoken dialogue system (SDS) usually needs a substantial amount of handcrafting or a well-labeled dataset to be trained on

problem.concept: we need a test for determining what are the morphemes of a language, or at least a test that would tentatively segment a phonemic sequence (as a sentence) into morphemes, leaving it for a distributional criterion to decide which of these tentative segments are to be accepted as morphemes

review_notes: Restored the tentative-segmentation alternative and the distributional acceptance criterion. The title supports a computer test, while the abstract supplies no explicit new finding or named corpus.

problem.concept: computation of boolean operations on polyhedra is almost always addressed by focusing on the case of two polyhedra
For large trees, this is both error prone due to intermediate geometry and error accumulation, and inefficient because each node yields a specific overhead

task.concept: polyhedral CSG evaluation, addressing the general N-polyhedron case

contribution.concept: QuickCSG
new vertex-centric view
output complexity depending on the output mesh size instead of the input size as with usual approaches
algorithm achieves breakthrough performance, one to two orders of magnitude speedups with respect to state-of-the-art CPU algorithms, on boolean operations over two to several dozen polyhedra
algorithm is also shown to outperform recent GPU implementations and approximate discretizations, while producing an exact output without redundant facets

review_notes: Added the explicit two-polyhedron scope gap motivating the general N-polyhedron approach. Preserved vertex-centric view, KD-tree pruning, task stealing, exact output and both CPU/GPU comparisons.
